answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded random walks, so voting influence depends on reachable, independently anchored attestations rather than identities alone. A sybil cluster isolated like an island has a sparse external cut and low conductance; over a fixed walk horizon, little probability flow crosses that boundary. Given bounded initial trust and normalized voting weights, this limits the cluster’s aggregate voting power, preventing it from reaching a summit by multiplying identities.
